subject: community-medicine
title: Nutritional Interventions: Rehabilitation Centres and Anemia Mukt Bharat

steps.title: Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres: inpatient care
steps.tx: Established at district and sub-district hospitals, the **Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre facility** provides specialized inpatient therapeutic care for children suffering from severe acute malnutrition with medical complications or failed appetite tests. A typical fourteen-day admission provides round-the-clock medical stabilization, therapeutic feeding with starter formula F-75 and catch-up formula F-100, sensory stimulation, and structured maternal counselling to prevent nutritional relapse after discharge.
steps.say: Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres admit severely malnourished children with infections for two weeks, feeding them therapeutic milk formulas and teaching mothers how to prepare nutritious home meals.

nodes.label: Transition phase: Increase feeds gradually (Days 3 to 7)
Rehabilitation phase: F-100 and catch-up growth

steps.tx: A bed in a nutrition centre, with the mother present for feeds, is inpatient care for complicated severe acute malnutrition. The **Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre facility** is placed at district and sub district hospitals. Admission is for children who have medical complications or who fail an appetite test. A typical stay of 14 days gives continuous stabilisation, starter formula F 75, catch up formula F 100, sensory stimulation, and counselling aimed at preventing relapse after discharge.
steps.say: Children with severe malnutrition plus complications, or those who will not eat, are admitted for about two weeks. They receive F 75 and then F 100, medical care, stimulation, and teaching so the mother can continue feeding at home.

steps.title: The ten steps of malnutrition management
steps.tx: Inpatient therapy adheres strictly to the standardized **ten steps of management**, divided into stabilization (days one to seven) and rehabilitation (weeks two to six). The critical first forty-eight hours focus on preventing and treating hypothermia, managing hypoglycemia with ten percent glucose, treating dehydration without intravenous fluid overload using ReSoMal (oral rehydration solution for malnutrition), restoring electrolyte balance with potassium and magnesium, and initiating broad-spectrum antibiotics.
steps.say: The ten steps begin by keeping the child warm, correcting low blood sugar, treating dehydration with specialized ReSoMal, fixing electrolytes, and giving broad-spectrum antibiotics.

rows: 10% glucose feed immediately; feed every 2 hours
Kangaroo mother care; maintain room temp 28-32 C
Oral ReSoMal slowly; avoid standard IV saline
Give potassium and magnesium; zero extra sodium
Routine ampicillin and gentamicin to all cases
Vitamin A, zinc, copper; delay iron until week 2

steps.title: Cautious feeding: F-75 versus F-100 formulas
steps.tx: During the initial stabilization phase, children are fed **F-75 starter therapeutic formula**, providing seventy-five kilocalories and zero point nine grams of protein per one hundred millilitres, designed to support basic cellular respiration without overwhelming fragile hepatic and renal capacities. Once appetite returns and oedema subsides, the child transitions to F-100 formula, providing one hundred kilocalories and two point nine grams of protein per decilitre to drive rapid catch-up growth.
steps.say: Children start on low-protein F-75 milk to prevent liver and heart failure. Once swelling clears and hunger returns, they switch to high-protein F-100 milk for rapid catch-up growth.

steps.title: Refeeding syndrome danger in early recovery
steps.tx: Clinicians must guard against the lethal threat of **refeeding syndrome**, which arises when aggressive high-carbohydrate feedings are introduced too rapidly into a severely malnourished child. Surging insulin drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly to support glycolysis and protein synthesis, producing severe hypophosphataemia, cardiac arrhythmias, acute congestive heart failure and sudden death, requiring slow, gradual calorie advancement.
steps.say: Feeding too much food too fast triggers refeeding syndrome. Surging insulin pulls potassium and phosphate out of the blood, causing fatal heart failure and sudden collapse.

nodes.label: Severe intracellular shift of phosphate and potassium

steps.tx: The cylinder and whisk are preparing starter formula, which must stay modest in calories at the beginning. **Refeeding syndrome** follows when carbohydrate is pushed too fast into a severely malnourished child. A surge of insulin drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells to support glycolysis and protein synthesis. Blood phosphate can fall sharply. Arrhythmias, acute heart failure, and sudden death may follow. Calories are advanced slowly even after appetite returns.
steps.say: Starter milk is kept limited because a sudden carbohydrate load in severe malnutrition drives insulin up and pulls phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells. The blood levels crash, and heart failure or sudden death can follow.

steps.title: Standard haemoglobin cut-offs for anaemia
steps.tx: Accurate clinical and community triage requires applying the established **WHO haemoglobin cut-offs** to diagnose and grade anaemia severity across diverse demographic cohorts. Anaemia is defined as haemoglobin below eleven grams per decilitre in pregnant women and children under five years, below eleven point five in children aged five to eleven, below twelve in non-pregnant adult women, and below thirteen grams per decilitre in adult men.
steps.say: Anaemia means haemoglobin below eleven grams per decilitre in pregnant mothers and young children, below twelve in non-pregnant women, and below thirteen in adult men.

steps.title: Anemia Mukt Bharat operational architecture
steps.tx: To reduce anaemia prevalence across India by three percentage points annually, the comprehensive **Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy** mobilises an intensified institutional network. Interventions combine prophylactic iron-folic acid supplementation, biannual deworming, testing and treatment at point of care using digital haemoglobinometers, mandatory food fortification of ration rice, and extensive behavior change communication promoting iron-rich dietary practices.
steps.say: The Anemia Mukt Bharat initiative tests blood with digital meters, dispenses iron tablets across age groups, deworms children twice a year, and fortifies ration rice with iron.

steps.title: Goitre survey methodology and endemicity grading
steps.tx: To determine whether a district requires targeted iodine intervention, epidemiologists conduct an **endemic goitre survey** among schoolchildren aged six to twelve years, examining thirty clusters of forty children using clinical thyroid palpation. Total Goitre Rate (TGR) combines Grade 1 (palpable thyroid lobes larger than the child's thumb terminal phalanx) and Grade 2 (visible goitre with neck in neutral position); TGR exceeding five percent confirms endemicity.
steps.say: Goitre surveys palpate thyroid glands in schoolchildren aged six to twelve. If more than five percent of surveyed children have an enlarged thyroid, the district is declared endemic.

rows: Thyroid lobes smaller than child's thumb
Thyroid palpable but not visible in neutral neck
Enlarged lobes match or exceed thumb phalanx
Goitre clearly visible with neck in normal position
Distinct neck mass visible from a distance

steps.title: National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme
steps.tx: The centrally assisted **NIDDCP operational mandate** enforces the production, transportation, and consumption of adequately iodised salt across India. The programme monitors salt samples using spot testing kits, conducts periodic resurveys every five years to validate goitre decline, and supports state health departments with dedicated iodine monitoring laboratories that test urinary iodine excretion to ensure biological sufficiency.
steps.say: The National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme tests salt quality across market shops and homes, verifying urine iodine levels to ensure complete eradication of cretinism.

nodes.label: Universal production of iodised salt (30 ppm)
Household salt testing by ASHA using test kits
District goitre resurveys every five years

steps.title: Double fortified salt: iron plus iodine
steps.tx: To tackle the dual epidemics of iron deficiency anaemia and iodine deficiency simultaneously, food technologists formulated **double fortified salt innovation**, which incorporates both potassium iodate and microencapsulated ferrous fumarate or ferric pyrophosphate into standard crystalline salt. Delivered through school meals and Anganwadi centres, it supplies one hundred percent of daily iodine and roughly thirty percent of daily iron requirements without altering taste or appearance.
steps.say: Double fortified salt incorporates both iodine and microencapsulated iron into table salt. Distributing this salt through school lunches tackles anaemia and goitre simultaneously.

left.title: Standard iodised salt
points: Has no effect on nutritional anaemia

right.title: Double fortified salt (DFS)
points: Prevents both goitre and iron deficiency anaemia
Supplies 30% of daily iron needs safely
